text:
marco: quick question — we need to pick a default strategy for onprem upgrades: streaming checkpoint + resumable apply vs full-image swap. streaming reduces bandwidth for large modelstores but complicates operator UX. any strong opinions?

olivia: streaming seems the right default for customers with limited egress. key is we must guarantee an atomic activation window. manifest needs an activation marker and a clear commit/rollback path. :thinking_face:

devon: +1 for streaming. practical concern: chunked checksums + resume tokens. power cut mid-apply -> partial-apply risk unless we have idempotent markers.

sre-bot: incident reference: partial-apply rollback caused last outage — see /incidents/342 for timeline and logs.

tanya: proposal to address partial-apply: add a small commit log alongside the manifest. operator writes per-component apply state (pending|applied|activated). on restart operator reconciles using that log so double-apply is detectable.

liam: can we avoid a heavy on-disk journal? maybe keep manifest-level version + per-component state in the operator CRD (k8s). that keeps disk footprint minimal and leverages etcd for durability.

marco: rough config sketch (for prototyping):
```yaml
operator:
  apply_window: 30m           # window for activation after apply
  resume_token_ttl: 24h      # how long a resume token is valid
  checkpoint_style: streaming
  checksum: blake3           # chosen for speed + small collison surface
  activation_policy: two_phase_commit
```

kevin: blake3 is a sensible default for content checks. also strongly prefer content-addressed block fetch so two different bundles dedupe on fetch-level. saves disk on constrained hosts.

olivia: UX note: when resume_token expires, operator should not restart silently. surface a "manual-restart" plan with the diff and required admin approval. we should also offer a dry-run mode so operators can preview actions before committing.

devon: tradeoff: two_phase_commit makes rollback logic more complex if operator restarts in the middle of phase two. we probably need a short-lived lease so only one operator instance can drive activation; otherwise we risk split-brain activation attempts.

marco: idea: ephemeral lease (k8s leader election) + signed activation marker created by a signer-sidecar after final verification. signer-sidecar writes a signed activation blob. fallback: if signer-sidecar absent (offline installs) operator can produce a local unsigned marker but mark cluster as requiring manual approval to activate.

tanya: how do we handle pure airgapped installs where streaming isn't possible (physical media like USB)? fallback should be seed-transfer + staged apply with compact diff format. offline signer workflow required.

liam: suggest a small protobuf delta format: patchlist + chunked payloads + per-chunk checksums. include signer chain metadata so an offline signer can sign the apply plan (not just the blobs). that lets the operator validate a signed sequence before applying.

marco: next concrete tasks: 1) update RFC with checkpoint token model and lease semantics; 2) add operator CRD fields for per-component apply state and resume token metadata; 3) prototype blake3 verification in signer-sidecar; 4) doc the manual-restart UX and dry-run.

kevin: +1 on tasks. tagging @oncall-sre for resilience scenarios and runbook updates. :white_check_mark:

oncall-sre: will add runbook entries for: resume_token expiry, partial-apply detection, manual-restart playbook. i will need sample logs and a branch with prototype to validate runbook steps.

marco: I'll spin a branch today and drop links here when ready. will include a small test harness that simulates powercut and resume. thanks everyone :rocket:
